import MumfordLib.GroupCohomologyCupOne
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Binomial

/-! # Vanishing of self-cup classes in integral group cohomology

The self-cup of an integral character is an integral coboundary.  The
primitive is the negative binomial coefficient, exactly as in the singular
cochain calculation.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

noncomputable section

namespace Mumford.Analytic

variable {U : Type} [AddCommGroup U]

private theorem choose_add_two (a b : ℤ) :
    Ring.choose (a + b) 2 = Ring.choose a 2 + a * b + Ring.choose b 2 := by
  rw [Ring.add_choose_eq 2 (Commute.all a b)]
  have h : Finset.antidiagonal 2 = {(0, 2), (1, 1), (2, 0)} := by decide
  rw [h]
  simp [add_comm]

/-- The integral primitive whose coboundary is the self-cup cocycle. -/
def groupCharacterSelfCupPrimitive (f : U →+ ℤ) : Multiplicative U → ℤ :=
  fun x => -Ring.choose (f x.toAdd) 2

theorem groupCharacterCupCocycle_self_mem_coboundaries (f : U →+ ℤ) :
    ((groupCharacterCupCocycle f f :
      groupCohomology.cocycles₂ (Rep.trivial ℤ (Multiplicative U) ℤ)) :
        Multiplicative U × Multiplicative U → ℤ) ∈
      groupCohomology.coboundaries₂ (Rep.trivial ℤ (Multiplicative U) ℤ) := by
  refine ⟨groupCharacterSelfCupPrimitive f, ?_⟩
  ext p
  rcases p with ⟨x, y⟩
  change f x.toAdd * f y.toAdd =
    (groupCohomology.d₁₂ (Rep.trivial ℤ (Multiplicative U) ℤ)
      (groupCharacterSelfCupPrimitive f)) (x, y)
  simp only [groupCohomology.d₁₂_hom_apply, Representation.isTrivial_apply]
  rw [map_add, choose_add_two]
  ring

theorem groupCharacterCupClass_self_eq_zero (f : U →+ ℤ) :
    groupCharacterCupClass f f = 0 := by
  change groupCohomology.H2π _ (groupCharacterCupCocycle f f) = 0
  rw [groupCohomology.H2π_eq_zero_iff]
  exact groupCharacterCupCocycle_self_mem_coboundaries f

end Mumford.Analytic
